layman_headline: Solana position is up 3% but the broader market just took a hit — patience is the play.
layman_explanation: The crypto market pulled back today with Bitcoin dropping nearly 3% after the Fed chair signaled more inflation-fighting work ahead. Our Solana position is still in profit (+3.1%) and recently got a bullish catalyst — validators just voted to accelerate SOL's supply reduction. However, the pullback across the board and high Bitcoin dominance (59%) make this a bad time to add new altcoin positions. The swing candidates on the watchlist are either already extended, lack technical data, or are stablecoins/gold tokens with no swing trade upside.
layman_action: Hold the current Solana position and wait. The stop-loss at $92 protects against a deeper drop, and the $115 target is still realistic if the disinflation catalyst plays out. Don't chase anything new right now.
expert_reasoning: The current swing candidates are poor quality: AKE is a micro-cap with a 67% daily pump and no technical data (classic chase trap), MON and PUMP are bleeding with no catalyst, PAXG/XAUT are gold-pegged stablecoins unsuitable for swing trading, and EURC/RLUSD are literal stablecoins. SOL's position is healthy at +3.1% unrealized with the disinflation vote providing fundamental support. The Fed's hawkish tone at Jackson Hole caused a broad risk-off move — BTC down 3%, most alts down 4-5%. BTC dominance at 59% continues to suppress altcoin performance. Better to wait for the selling pressure to exhaust before adding new positions. The Fear & Greed index dropping from 73 to 68 confirms cooling sentiment but isn't yet at levels that create strong buying opportunities.
risk_factors: Fed hawkishness could trigger further risk-off selling, pushing SOL below the $100 psychological level
BTC dominance at 59% continues to drain capital from altcoins — SOL could underperform even if crypto stabilizes
SOL's 10.4% weekly gain may need to consolidate further before resuming upward — a retest of $98-100 is possible
watch_list: BTC price action around $77,000-78,000 support — a breakdown here would drag all alts lower
SOL holding above $100 as psychological and technical support after the pullback
Follow-up commentary from Fed officials after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks
market_context: The market is in a risk-off mode following Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech emphasizing unfinished inflation work. BTC dominance at 59% signals capital rotating to Bitcoin safety, making altcoin entries particularly risky right now.
context_banner: Fed hawkishness triggers broad crypto pullback — hold existing SOL position with its disinflation catalyst, but no new entries warranted until selling pressure subsides.

key_signals.description: Fear & Greed dropped from 73 to 68 (Greed) — cooling but not yet at contrarian buy levels, suggesting more downside possible before a clean setup emerges.
Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole stated 'we have work to do' on inflation, triggering risk-off selling across crypto with BTC dropping to $78.4K.
Solana validators approved a proposal to accelerate SOL disinflation, a structurally bullish supply-reduction catalyst supporting the current position.
No compelling volume breakout patterns among swing candidates — AKE's 67% pump lacks reliable volume data and smells like a pump-and-dump.
RSI data unavailable for all swing candidates this cycle, making it impossible to identify oversold bounce setups with confidence.
